criteria.no: A decisive term is a subjective quality, an undefined label or mode, an unidentified expected output or standard, or an approval with no identified record.
criteria.unclear: A term may not be understood, but it cannot be told whether it is decisive.
criteria.yes: Every decisive term can be understood from the statement or common technical knowledge.

self_contained.instructions: Can each decisive term in `anchor.statement` be understood from the statement itself or from common technical knowledge? Understood terms include commands, subcommands, flags, files, paths, commit hashes, error and diagnostic codes, report and record ids, values, environment variables, formats, streams, roles such as 'the caller', and terms the statement defines inline. Bundled duties, added details, sentence form, and who is told to act (a named component, 'you', or nobody) do not matter here. A term cannot be understood when it is a subjective quality (robust), a label, tier, or mode the statement never defines (R7, Mode K), even when it appears among concrete records,, an expected output or standard whose record the statement does not identify, or a person's approval with no identified record.

anchor.statement: The package may publish only when the release lead approves.
anchor.quote: only publish after the release lead says yes
